params.script_inline:
import sys, json, os

# The member's export sink. Every hive of this member that carries a transfer
# lane walks its own tables and hands out one `dump` part per table; each part
# is a whole document part -- schema plus rows -- and the receiving side's
# README says what to do with it: "write {"schema": ...} as line 1 and one row
# per line after it and you have a seed/<table>.jsonl". That is exactly what
# this cell does, and it is the whole reason the lane has a drain at all: a
# document that only ever existed as messages is not a backup. The boundary is
# the sandbox write root, not this script -- everything below lands under
# params.export_dir and nowhere else.
#
# ONE DIRECTORY PER HIVE (GH #471). A part names the hive it came out of
# (`hive_template`), and that name is the directory it is filed under. Before
# #471 the memory hive was the only sender and everything landed flat, which
# stopped working the moment a second sender existed: `memory-hive` and
# `affinity` both have a table called `entities`, and a flat sink would have
# written one over the other without a word.

doc = json.load(sys.stdin)
body = doc.get("body") or {}
params = doc.get("params") or {}
header = (doc.get("envelope") or {}).get("header") or {}
hop = header.get("hop") or {}

EXPORT_DIR = str(params.get("export_dir") or "")
MARKER = "export_final.json"
MEMBER_FORMAT = "meclaw-member-export/1"


def fail(code, text):
    sys.stdout.write(json.dumps({
        "header": {"route": "error", "error_code": code, "finish_reason": "error"},
        "messages": [{"origin": "assistant", "type": "text", "text": text}]}))
    sys.exit(0)


def nothing():
    sys.stdout.write(json.dumps([]))
    sys.exit(0)


def plain_name(value):
    """A name that may become a directory or a file, and nothing else."""
    return bool(value) and os.path.basename(value) == value and not value.startswith(".")


if not EXPORT_DIR:
    fail("invalid_input", "params.export_dir is empty -- an export sink without a directory is a drain that drops")

# An import receipt rides the same lane (hop.dump_kind) and belongs to whoever
# asked for the import. The drain edge has to be a PLAIN route test, so the
# receipt arrives here; ignoring it is a decision, not an oversight.
if str(hop.get("dump_kind") or "export_part") != "export_part":
    nothing()

msgs = body.get("messages") or []
if not msgs:
    fail("invalid_input", "a dump part travels as the text of its one turn, and this message had no turn")
try:
    part = json.loads(msgs[0].get("text") or "")
except Exception as exc:
    fail("invalid_input", "the dump part is not JSON: %s" % exc)
if not isinstance(part, dict) or not part.get("table"):
    fail("invalid_input", "the dump part names no table")

table = str(part.get("table"))
if not plain_name(table):
    fail("invalid_input", "a table name is a file name here, and this one is not: %s" % table)

# The hive is the directory. A part that does not name one cannot be filed
# without guessing which sender it belongs to, and guessing is how one hive's
# `entities` ends up in another's seed set.
hive = str(part.get("hive_template") or "")
if not plain_name(hive):
    fail("invalid_input",
         "the dump part names no hive (`hive_template`), and the sink files a part under "
         "the hive it came out of: %r" % hive)

HIVE_DIR = os.path.join(EXPORT_DIR, hive)
SEED_DIR = os.path.join(HIVE_DIR, "seed")


def hive_marker(directory):
    """The completeness marker of one hive, or None if that hive has not
    finished (or was never here)."""
    try:
        with open(os.path.join(EXPORT_DIR, directory, "seed", MARKER)) as fh:
            found = json.load(fh)
    except (OSError, ValueError):
        return None
    return found if isinstance(found, dict) else None


def rewrite_member_marker():
    """The member-level marker, rebuilt from what stands on disk.

    It is rebuilt rather than appended to, every time a hive finishes, because
    a marker that says which parts an export HAS must be derived from the parts
    that are there -- an appended list survives a directory somebody emptied and
    keeps claiming a completeness the tree does not have. Rebuilding is also
    what makes a second, later export of one hive into the same directory
    correct rather than additive.
    """
    parts = []
    for entry in sorted(os.listdir(EXPORT_DIR)):
        if not os.path.isdir(os.path.join(EXPORT_DIR, entry)):
            continue
        found = hive_marker(entry)
        if found is None:
            continue
        parts.append({"hive": entry, "format": found.get("format"),
                      "export_id": found.get("export_id"),
                      "exported_at": found.get("exported_at"),
                      "of": found.get("of"),
                      "seed_dir": found.get("seed_dir")})
    with open(os.path.join(EXPORT_DIR, MARKER), "w") as fh:
        fh.write(json.dumps({"format": MEMBER_FORMAT, "export_dir": EXPORT_DIR,
                             "hives": [p["hive"] for p in parts], "parts": parts},
                            sort_keys=True) + "\n")
    return parts


try:
    # `<hive>/seed/` is created; the write ROOT is not, because the sandbox has
    # to be able to grant it before this script runs at all.
    os.makedirs(SEED_DIR, exist_ok=True)
    # An absent table writes no file: `absent` says this hive never had the
    # table, and an empty seed file would claim it had one and remembered
    # nothing. `rows: []` is that second thing, and it DOES get a file.
    if not part.get("absent"):
        lines = [json.dumps({"schema": part.get("schema") or {}}, sort_keys=True)]
        for row in part.get("rows") or []:
            lines.append(json.dumps(row, sort_keys=True))
        path = os.path.join(SEED_DIR, table + ".jsonl")
        tmp = path + ".part"
        with open(tmp, "w") as fh:
            fh.write("\n".join(lines) + "\n")
        os.replace(tmp, path)

    final = bool(part.get("final")) or str(hop.get("export_final") or "0") == "1"
    if not final:
        nothing()

    # The hive's own marker is written after the last part's own file, in the
    # same run, so it can never claim a completeness the directory does not
    # have. That is what params.max_concurrency = 1 buys: the parts arrive in
    # walk order and one finishes before the next begins.
    with open(os.path.join(SEED_DIR, MARKER), "w") as fh:
        fh.write(json.dumps({"format": part.get("format"),
                             "hive": hive,
                             "export_id": part.get("export_id"),
                             "exported_at": part.get("exported_at"),
                             "of": part.get("of"),
                             "seed_dir": SEED_DIR}, sort_keys=True) + "\n")
    # ... and only then the member-level one, which names every hive that has
    # finished so far. Four hives are four walks and four completion words, and
    # nothing here waits for the others: an export is complete for the hives it
    # lists, and the list is the honest answer at every point in between.
    hives = rewrite_member_marker()
except OSError as exc:
    fail("io_error", "the export sink could not write under %s: %s" % (SEED_DIR, exc))

sys.stdout.write(json.dumps({
    "header": {"route": "export_done",
               "export_id": str(part.get("export_id") or ""),
               "export_hive": hive,
               "export_of": int(part.get("of") or 0),
               "seed_dir": SEED_DIR},
    "messages": [{"origin": "assistant", "type": "text",
                  "text": json.dumps({"seed_dir": SEED_DIR,
                                      "export_dir": EXPORT_DIR,
                                      "hive": hive,
                                      "parts": int(part.get("of") or 0),
                                      "hives_done": [h["hive"] for h in hives],
                                      "marker": MARKER}, sort_keys=True)}]}))

export_dir.description: Directory the exports are written under; it must exist before an export is triggered, because it is also the sandbox write root and a root that is not there fails the spawn closed. One subdirectory per exporting hive lands in it (`memory-hive`, `affinity`, `firewall`, and `session-keeper` when a generation was named) -- `<hive>/seed/<table>.jsonl` plus `<hive>/seed/export_final.json` -- beside the member-level `export_final.json`; every one of those this cell does create.

description.purpose: The one cell that turns this member's exports from a stack of messages into files. Every hive of this member that carries a transfer lane -- `memory-hive`, `affinity` and `firewall` since member@1.5.0, plus the session keeper of a NAMED generation since GH #475 -- walks its own tables and hands out one `dump` part per table. This cell files each part under the hive it came out of: `<export_dir>/<hive>/seed/<table>.jsonl`, the schema declaration as line 1 and one row per line after it, which is the birth format every one of those stores reads. The last part of a hive additionally writes `<hive>/seed/export_final.json` and rewrites the member-level `<export_dir>/export_final.json`, which names every hive that has finished; only then does the level say `export_done` for that hive.
description.use_when: Never on its own -- it travels with member@1.5.0 and is fed by one edge per exporting hive, each a plain `hop.route == 'dump'` test; the fourth of them takes the lane off `./assistants` rather than off a holder, because the keeper stands inside a generation (GH #475). The plainness is a requirement rather than a style: every one of those hives pairs `in_export` with `dump` in its `required_drains`, and the probe that checks the pairing runs the described hop through the real edge evaluator, so an edge that additionally tested `hop.dump_kind` would read as no drain at all and refuse the mutation. Point `MEMBER_EXPORT_DIR` at the directory you want the seed sets in, and create it before you trigger an export; the per-hive subdirectories are created here.
description.not_in_scope: It writes; it does not decide. What may leave a hive is that hive's own walk and no business of this level -- there is no filter here, no audience test and no second copy of any export format. It does not merge either: one hive is one directory, and the reason is measurable rather than tidy -- `memory-hive` and `affinity` both have a table called `entities`, so a flat sink would write one over the other without a word (GH #471). One hive is one directory in the other direction too, and that is why the member NAMES the generation whose keeper it wants (GH #475): two generations of one person hold two session ledgers under one hive name, and a sink that filed both would keep whichever walk finished last and say nothing about the other. It is not a `file` cell, and that is a choice with a reason: a `file` cell canonicalizes its `base_path` in `validate_params`, so a member whose export directory did not exist would fail `--validate` and BOOT, for a lane nobody has used yet. The sandbox write root is the same boundary one message later, where a missing directory is a routed `io_error` instead of a dead colony. It also does not read a document back: an import is each hive's own lane, and an `import_receipt` arriving here is ignored rather than filed.
